comment: Repo-side freshness pins for every citation in signoff/block-manifest.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `klt signoff --manifest` compares a manifest's
`content_hash` against the *cited envelope's own* claim about its input --
it never opens the underlying artifact. klt 0.6.0 says so itself, on every
pinned citation: `input: not re-hashed (content_hash compared against this
envelope's own claim only -- the artifact itself was not read)`. Two
hand-written files agreeing with each other proves nothing, so this file
records the sha256 of the artifact each citation is really about, and
signoff/check.sh re-hashes it on disk in CI. That is what makes a citation
here fail rather than rot when its artifact moves.
As of issue #127 every citation in the manifest carries a manifest pin;
none is structurally unpinnable any more. Item 6 was the last holdout --
its Monte Carlo envelope was produced by klt 0.2.0
(layout/requirements.txt's *original* pin), which wrote
`provenance.input: null`, and a manifest `content_hash` against an
envelope that claims no input hash renders the item unmet/stale_evidence
-- a false negative. #127 re-pointed it at the campaign's current record
(`20260925-131502-808cece`), whose `provenance.input.content_hash` is
real, so the manifest pins it directly and this file's entry is now the
second, independent on-disk check rather than the only one.
Issue #203 then moved item 6's citation again -- from that campaign
response to a `klt yield` report over it, the evidence KIND the item
actually names -- which changes what `klt signoff` hashes for this item. A
`klt yield` report carries no `provenance` block, so the grader hashes the
samples document the report names instead (docs/cli/signoff.md).
Issue #211 then added the deterministic negative control item 6's own
checklist text asks for, which moves that hashed samples document one
level up. `klt sim` cannot express a `negative_control` on its own
response (2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2563), and hand-editing a committed
response is not available under sim/README.md's append-only discipline, so
sim/bin/yield-run.py --negative-control mints a DERIVED sample-set
document -- the nominal campaign's per-sample values plus the seeded
known-bad variant's -- and `klt yield` analyses that. Item 6 therefore has
five entries below: the derived sample-set document as the manifest-pinned
one, and four unpinned on-disk claims underneath it -- the nominal
campaign response and the negative control's response (each cross-checked
against the derived document's own `provenance` block, so the pin cannot
be re-pointed at a different pair of runs than the report analysed), plus
each campaign's netlist snapshot. Nothing about this arrangement asks a
reader to trust the derivation: yield-run.py independently re-runs
`klt yield` over the nominal response alone and requires identical nominal
statistics before it will write anything.
Item 4's LVS citation no longer needs that workaround either (issue #127):
it was re-pointed at the current klt 0.6.0 record
(`20260924-221912-a947aa8`, the one `layout/ldo-core/reports/LATEST-LVS`
names) whose `provenance.input.content_hash` is
non-null, so the manifest now pins it directly. Its two entries below
stay anyway -- `environment.layout_sha256`/`environment.reference_sha256`
are a second, independent claim the manifest pin alone does not cover
(same discipline item 3's and item 7's entries below apply).
`envelope_field` is a dotted path into the cited envelope whose value must
equal `sha256`; null means the envelope makes no hash claim about this
artifact and only the on-disk re-hash is checked.

pins.note: The composed LDO-core GDS the `klt drc` run read. Also the manifest's own item-3 pin, so all three -- file on disk, envelope claim, manifest pin -- must agree.

Re-pinned by issue #127 against the klt 0.6.0 re-run's own copy of the composed LDO-core GDS (previously klt 0.2.0's 20260825-123628-3b4e121, whose lvs envelope carried no provenance.input at all). Specifically the *current* such record, 20260924-221912-a947aa8 -- the one layout/ldo-core/reports/LATEST-LVS names. The earlier klt 0.6.0 re-run 20260924-181216-50554fe (PR #155) would satisfy the provenance requirement identically, but it predates commit 0c65db2 (#163, VIN/VOUT sized as spec-derived power rails), which redrew the layout and produced this record; citing 50554fe would pin item 4 to a layout revision main has already superseded. The two lvs.json envelopes are byte-identical apart from the layout hash -- same status: match, same three warning-severity mismatches, same power_connectivity/body_verification blocks -- so this is a citation-currency fix, not a result change. This GDS is not byte-identical to item 3's still-3b4e121-vintage GDS -- item 3 was not in #127's scope -- so this hash is checked only against this envelope's own environment.layout_sha256 and, now, the manifest's own item-4 content_hash pin (provenance.input.content_hash == environment.layout_sha256 on this record, so both agree on one value).

The schematic-derived reference netlist the layout was compared against -- item 4 requires the compare to be against item 1's netlist, so the reference side needs pinning too, not just the layout side. Re-pinned by issue #127 alongside the GDS entry above; the manifest pin covers only the layout (input) side, not this reference side.

The sample set the cited `klt yield` report analyses -- and, for a yield citation, the artifact `klt signoff` itself hashes (`report["samples"]`, resolved relative to the report's own directory first; docs/cli/signoff.md, '`klt yield` evidence and content hashing'). `envelope_field` is null because a yield report makes no hash claim to cross-check, so this entry is a direct on-disk re-hash and the manifest pins the same value. WHAT KIND OF DOCUMENT THIS IS, AND WHY IT CHANGED WITH #211: through issue #203 this was the Monte Carlo campaign response itself (`20260925-131502-808cece.json`). Issue #211 added the deterministic negative control item 6's own checklist text asks for, and a `negative_control` is metadata on a measurement that `klt sim` has no way to express -- its Monte Carlo request has no field for one and its response rollup never emits one -- so a klt sim response can only carry a negative control if a committed response is hand-edited, which sim/README.md's append-only discipline forbids outright. Filed upstream, generically, as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2563. `sim/bin/yield-run.py --negative-control` therefore mints a derived SAMPLE-SET document instead: the nominal campaign's own per-sample values plus the control's, extracted by the same rule `klt yield` applies to a sim report itself, committed and append-only like every other artifact here. Both campaign responses behind it are pinned in their own entries below, and the derived document's own `provenance` block is what cross-checks them. The extraction is not taken on trust: yield-run.py runs `klt yield` a second time directly over the nominal response (the pre-#211 input shape) and requires the nominal distribution/capability/sample-size/empirical-yield blocks to be byte-equal, aborting rather than recording on any difference -- that check reads IDENTICAL in the cited record. WHAT THE REPORT SAYS: status=reported, 1 measurement, `vout_ss` n=200 against the ratified 1.764-1.836 V window -- empirical yield 100% (Clopper-Pearson CI 98.1725%-100% at 95% confidence, i.e. 'at least 98.1725%', not '100% yield'), normal-fit 99.9968% (CI 99.9911%-100%), Anderson-Darling normality 'consistent', Cp 1.40797 / Cpk 1.34664 (CI 1.20651-1.48677), sigma-to-spec 4.03992 (CI 3.61952-4.46032, limiting side upper), sample size 'sufficient' (observed CI half-width 0.00913767 against a 0.01 target, required_n 183) -- and, new with #211, `negative_control.verdict: detected`: the seeded known-bad variant's own empirical yield is 0% (CP CI 0%-8.8097%, n=40) against the nominal's CP interval of 98.1725%-100%, two intervals that do not overlap. ONE DISCLOSURE THE GRADER STILL CANNOT MAKE, in signoff/README.md -> 'Item 6 is met -- what it says, and the one thing it does not': status is `reported`, not `pass`, because no measurement declares a `target_yield` -- spec/target-spec.md ratifies no yield or sigma target for this block -- and `klt signoff` accepts `reported` as passing on the stated ground that nothing could fail. So item 6's `met` says the statistical evidence of the required kind exists, is sound, is negative-control-checked and is pinned; it does not say a yield claim was checked. Declaring such a target is a `spec/` decision record, not a manifest edit. The negative-control half of that disclosure is CLOSED by #211 and is not restated as open.

The nominal Monte Carlo campaign response -- the N=200 campaign of record whose per-sample `vout_ss` values are the numerator and denominator of every statistic in the cited report. It was the manifest's own item-6 pin from issue #203 until #211, which re-pointed the pin one level up to the derived sample-set document (see the entry above), demoting this to a second, independent on-disk claim -- the same discipline items 3, 4 and 7 apply. Unlike the netlist-snapshot entry below, this one has a real `envelope_field`: the derived document records where each leg came from, so `provenance.nominal.sha256` is a hash claim to cross-check rather than an unpinnable dependency. Re-pinning the derived document without re-deriving it from this exact response therefore fails here.

The SEEDED, KNOWN-BAD variant's own campaign response (issue #211) -- the other half of the cited report's sample set, and the thing that makes item 6's `negative_control` clause evidence rather than an assumption. A deliberately degraded campaign: `sim/mc-output-accuracy-negctl` is the nominal bench verbatim (same testbench schematic, referenced not copied; same tt_mm/27C/VIN=3.3V mismatch point; same #164 `uic` initial-condition contract; same `vout_ss` measurement against the same UNRELAXED ratified 1.764-1.836 V window; same seed 20260817) with exactly one declared defect: the feedback divider's top leg XR_FB_A lengthened 180um -> 198um (+10%), which moves the ideal regulation point 1.8 V -> 1.86 V. Its own aggregate status is FAIL, and that is the intended result -- a control exists to be rejected. Cross-checked here against the derived document's `provenance.negative_control.sha256`, so the report cannot be re-pinned against a different control run than the one it analysed.

The DEGRADED deck the negative control actually ran on (issue #211). Pinned for the same reason the nominal campaign's netlist snapshot is pinned below: a statistical claim is only as good as the certainty about which circuit produced it, and here that matters more than usual, because the whole evidentiary value of a negative control rests on the deck differing from the nominal's in exactly the one declared way. It does, and it is checkable without trusting any prose: this deck differs from the campaign of record's committed snapshot (`sha256:e760a7c3...`, pinned below) in a single line, the XR_FB_A resistor instance, which is also what `sim/mc-output-accuracy-negctl/experiment.json`'s `netlist_patch` declares and what the record's before/after deck hashes record. The patch is applied by `sim/bin/mc-run.py` to the netlisted deck between xschem and `klt sim` as an exact-string substitution with an ASSERTED occurrence count -- so `design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch` stays the single source of truth for the design under test, no frozen duplicate of it can rot alongside, and if the divider in the real design ever changes the count stops matching and the campaign refuses to run rather than quietly sampling an undegraded circuit and reporting it as a negative control.

The netlist the NOMINAL Monte Carlo campaign ran on -- and, as of issue #211, the deck the negative control's degraded deck is a one-line variant of, so the two entries above read against this one. NO LONGER THE MANIFEST'S OWN ITEM-6 PIN as of issue #203: item 6 cites a `klt yield` report rather than the campaign response itself, and `klt signoff` hashes a yield citation's *samples document* rather than anything the netlist appears in, so the manifest pin moved away from here and this stays as an independent on-disk claim -- the same discipline items 3, 4 and 7 apply. (Issue #211 moved that pin once more, from the campaign response to the derived sample-set document; see the first item-6 entry above. This entry is unaffected either way.) Everything below is the #127-era history of this entry, unchanged and still true of the campaign the yield report analyses. Re-pointed by issue #127 from the klt 0.2.0 record 20260825-083111-4cb27f8, whose sim envelope wrote provenance.input: null and named the netlist only by an absolute path from the machine that produced it, so no manifest pin was possible and this on-disk hash was the citation's only freshness handle. The current record carries a real provenance.input.content_hash (identical to its own environment.netlist_sha256), so the manifest pins it directly and this entry cross-checks it on disk. WHICH record, and what changed with it: 4cb27f8 is twice superseded -- 20260925-110312-8280915 supersedes it and 20260925-131502-808cece supersedes that, per each record's own Supersedes field -- so 4cb27f8 was no longer the campaign of record for this block at all; measurements/characterization.md's Output row already cites 808cece. The intermediate 8280915 (status=error, 185 pass / 12 fail / 3 error of 200) would have kept item 6's klt-signoff reason at check_failed, but citing a record its own successor replaces, in order to keep a reason token steady, is not a freshness pin -- it is the opposite of one. 808cece is the campaign's current, correct result after issue #164 fixed the bench's initial-condition contract: status=pass, 200/200, vout_ss mean 1.80157 V inside the ratified 1.764-1.836 V window with a 3-sigma window of [1.776, 1.82714]. Item 6's verdict does NOT change -- it was unmet before and is unmet now, and t1_met_count stays 3 -- but its graded reason moves check_failed -> wrong_kind, because the cited check no longer fails on its own terms and item 6 asks specifically for a klt yield report, which does not exist for this campaign (docs/cli/signoff.md). That is a more accurate machine-readable statement of this block's position, not a weaker one: the statistical evidence is now a passing campaign with no yield report over it, where before it was a failing campaign measured on a bench with a known, since-fixed defect. Disclosed in full in signoff/README.md -> 'Item 6 is met -- what it says, and the one thing it does not' (titled '...the two things...' until issue #211 closed the negative-control half) -> 'How item 6 got here' (that section was retitled by #203 when the item stopped citing the campaign directly; the #127 narrative it carried is preserved there as the subsection).
The `klt pex` run's input layout -- the same composed GDS items 3 and 4 were run on, which is what makes the (errored) post-layout leg comparable to them at all.
The extracted netlist the post-layout re-simulation was attempted against.

The aggregated per-spec-row rollup the generic envelope wraps. Regenerating it (measurements/build_characterization_report.py) without re-pinning here fails CI, which is the point: item 8 asks for a *current* artifact. Re-pinned by issue #142, by issue #154, and again by issue #118 (which re-ran the Output, Line regulation and Load regulation rows in full against the post-#116 DUT: all three rows' cited record ids change and all three flip STALE -> fresh, while all three verdicts stay FAIL -- the rollup is still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS / 4 N/A, so this envelope's own summary is unchanged). The two earlier re-pins -- both re-cut the DRC/LVS/PEX records the rollup's freshness table cites, and neither touched its 12 graded spec rows (still 9 FAIL / 3 PASS, as the envelope's summary says). #154's re-cut also flips the PEX detail line from status=pass to status=fail, which is the request declaring limits for the first time rather than a result getting worse -- see sim/pex-post-layout/README.md. Re-pinned again by issue #164, which changed sim/mc-output-accuracy's initial-condition contract (`tran ... uic`, EN as an edge) after measuring that the pre-#164 unconstrained `.op` handed 12 of 200 mismatch draws a start state that is not a circuit state (FB hundreds of volts ABOVE the VOUT node feeding it through a passive divider). The Output row's cited record becomes 20260925-131502-808cece and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see design/README.md "#164". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place rather than regenerated: `uvx --from klayout-tools==0.6.0` on the sweep host resolves to a git build (0.6.0+g983394050cff) whose grading_ruleset_id and item texts differ from the pinned release, so `check.sh --write` there would rewrite the yardstick instead of the evidence move. `content_hash` is the only field a faithful pinned regeneration changes. Re-pinned again by issue #180, which brought sim/load-transient into conformance with the same initial-condition contract (#171) #164 established: its `tran 200n 3m` now releases from an eleven-node `.ic`-constrained operating point instead of an unconstrained loop-closed `.op`, and the bench was re-run over the full 45-corner PVT matrix. The Load transient row's cited record becomes 20260926-013955-6449a98 and its Freshness flips STALE -> fresh, but its verdict stays FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and the envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. The row's own numbers did move: 0/45 corners PASS against the superseded record's 25/45, because that record predates #119 and measured neither the recovery-time clause (all 45 new failures) nor the 4.7uF C_out; the peak-excursion clause it did measure now passes at every corner. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "`load-transient` after #180". Re-pinned again by issue #179, which converted sim/loop-gain and sim/psrr-dc to the initial-condition contract's .nodeset-seeded .ac shape (#171) and re-ran both 45-corner matrices: the PSRR row's cited record becomes 20260926-033606-4a9ec09 and the Stability row's 20260926-040338-4a9ec09, and both rows flip STALE -> fresh (their predecessors predate #116/#139's pass-device resize). BOTH VERDICTS STAY FAIL, so this rollup is still 8 FAIL / 4 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is unchanged. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#179". Re-pinned again by issue #189, which closed the two corners sim/thermal still had on the #171 solver-diagnostic gate after #178's seeding: one of the thirteen nodes in its `.nodeset` card (EA_TAIL, the error amplifier's PMOS input-pair source node) was written `'vsup'`-relative although three cold-start settles at ss/80C -- one per supply on the corner axis -- put its supply slope at 0.24 V/V, so the card sat 288 mV below the real node at vsup = 2.97 V. Correcting the classification (same measured number, absolute instead of `{vsup-0.836}`) takes the bench to 15/15 PASS with 0 of 15 corner logs carrying a diagnostic. The Thermal row's cited record becomes 20260926-095154-f6ab418 and its verdict moves FAIL -> PASS, so this rollup is now 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary is updated to match. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#189". signoff/records/t1-tier-report.json carries the same new hash on its item-8 citation, edited in place for the reason #164's note records above. Re-pinned again by issue #187, which corrected sim/dropout-vs-load's supply convention: that bench was the only one in sim/ driving EN off the VIN rail (VIN pinned at 3.63V for every corner while 'vsup' drove EN alone), which put EN 0.66V below VIN at the '*_2.97v' corners and, at fs/125C, left the VIN-sourced shutdown clamps M_ENP/M_ENP2 conducting 1.377uA/1.639uA against a 39pA/62pA leakage floor -- more than the error amplifier's whole 1.003uA tail current, so EA_OUT was pulled to VIN and the block never came up. EN now tracks VIN and the ramp's endpoint tracks 'vsup' so its rate stays the constant 266.3 V/s earlier records ran at. The Dropout row's cited record becomes 20260926-102849-0b63ae4 and stays fresh; its VERDICT STAYS FAIL (0/45, 0.32997-0.67307V against the 300mV bound, the largest per-corner change being 0.010mV), so this rollup is still 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A and this envelope's own summary needs no edit -- only `content_hash` moves. What did change is that the row's evidence no longer reports a failing vout_at_max_vin_v corner: the -7.4521V reading at fs_125c_2.97v was the bench convention, not the design. No ratified bound and no DUT change -- see sim/README.md "#187". Re-pinned again by issue #196, which fixed the LAST bench carrying the same EN-below-VIN geometry: sim/line-regulation drove EN at the corner runner's 'vsup' while its own VVIN was 'alter'ed 2.97-3.63V inside every corner, so the VIN=3.63V point of every *_2.97v corner ran with EN 0.66V below VIN. EN now tracks the instantaneous VIN. Unlike #187 this one does NOT move a record: #196 committed the corrected deck but could not hold the ~7h serial 45-corner re-run on the sweep host (measured: 578.9s for one corner against 41.7s in the cited record), so the Line regulation row still cites 20260926-001833-228fbc7 and its FRESHNESS FLIPS fresh -> STALE -- the row's verdict, its cited record id and the 7 FAIL / 5 PASS / 4 N/A rollup are all unchanged, and this envelope's summary needs no edit; only `content_hash` moves. Re-pinned once more by #196's second increment (#200), which closed exactly that gap: the 45-corner matrix WAS run under the new convention on a host that could hold it (3914.8s serial, 306.7s worst corner) and record 20260926-200304-35b7392 supersedes 20260926-001833-228fbc7.
